title: Exercise Controller (MGySgt to Cpl) EMOS (0211, 0231, 0311, 0331, 0341, 0369, 0399, 0491, 0629, 0679, 0699, 0848, 1371, 1391, 2311, 2611, 2621, 2651, 3529, 3537, 7011), CG TECOM
raw_text:
18. MOS 0987, Exercise Controller (MGySgt to Cpl) EMOS (0211, 0231, 0311,
0331, 0341, 0369, 0399, 0491, 0629, 0679, 0699, 0848, 1371, 1391, 2311, 2611,
2621, 2651, 3529, 3537, 7011), CG TECOM

    a. Summary. Marines assigned to a teaching billet or faculty position
that facilitate learning as their primary duty who teach a designated course
approved by the appropriate general/flag officer in the chain of command.
Augmented personnel support used as training aids (e.g. role players,
demonstrator cadre) for instruction are not categorized as instructors.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2)   Fully qualified in the primary MOS aligned with the instructor
billet.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Completion of the locally executed, TECOM approved, service-level
instructor course(s) or other service instructor course.

        (2) EMOS approval authority is only by O-6 level commanding officer/
director under MAGTFTC.

            (3) Serve in a specified MAGTF instructor designated billet.

        (4) Serve as MAGTF instructor for one-year, however, and this is
waiverable only by O-6 level commanding/director under MAGTFTC.

        (5) CG, MAGTFTC will be the approving authority for all waivers where
marines are not currently assigned to fill a designated Instructor billet BIC
or any other request which does not meet the requirements listed above.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Instruct, assess, and mentor exercise participants at the
commensurate level of Marine Corps experience and occupational specialty
under the most realistic conditions possible.

        (2) Develop training objectives, concept cards, event handbooks, and
specific training event content applicable to service-level training
exercises appropriate to achieving the program and student learning outcomes.

        (3) Conduct research and professional development in areas of
competency to support training and education programs.

        (4) Participate in various standardization boards, rehearsals (range
walks, map drills, communication rehearsals, scheme of maneuver briefs), and
working groups that deal with academic matters and academic policy issues,
thereby creating an atmosphere of shared governance.




                                          3-105                       Enclosure (1)
 3115                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



        (5) Provide input into the decision-making and policy-making aspects
of the training and education continuum.

        (6) Develop and deliver curricula, lecture, instruct, facilitate
discussions and practical applications, and conduct field performance
critiques prior to departure from training events.

        (7) Review and provide updates to the Control Group’s standing
operating procedures.

        (8) Receive, analyze, and provide refinements to Scheme of Maneuver
briefs from exercise participants prior to execution of training events.

        (9) Advise exercise participants on the technical application of
doctrinal publications, reference publications, published service manuals,
and standing operating procedures with a focus on live-fire combined arms
operations.

        (10) Collaborate and share professional experiences and previous
observations with exercise participants to enhance learning and performance
to reverse negative trends across the service.

        (11) Master control procedures and develop instructional techniques
that will enhance participants’ ability to achieve particular training
objectives.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.




                                         3-106                   Enclosure (1)
 3116                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
